title: The first delivery between agents
dek: The tool finds {deliveries} write-then-read deliveries in the release. Only {named} are between named tokens, and {inside} of those stay inside one estimated agent. None shows the reader using what was written. Counting agents moves the first delivery between agents by more than a day.

deliveries.label: write-then-read deliveries in the release (a read of a place after a different actor wrote it)

named_pairs.label: sender and receiver pairs of named tokens

inside.label: deliveries between two tokens of one estimated agent

agent_a_confidence.label: confidence of the weakest merge in Agent A

share_tok.label: of the dated harmful actions came after the first delivery, counting tokens

share_agent.label: of the dated harmful actions came after the first delivery, counting estimated agents

audited.label: named deliveries read by one reader, the authors' AI assistant (not a person by hand)

audited_true.label: of them judged a real write and a later read of the same place

uses.label: deliveries where the reader's record shares what the writer wrote

body.p: The release is a set of code payloads and responses. Nothing in it says that one agent sent something to another. So the tool looks for something weaker. [[c1|One record writes to a shared place. Later, a record from a different actor reads the same place.]] The tool calls that a delivery. Earlier versions called it a message, which says too much. It shows the reader could have seen the write. It does not show that it did, and [[c13|in {uses} of the {deliveries} the reader's record shares anything the writer wrote.]]

[[c2|On the whole release the tool finds {deliveries} deliveries.]] An earlier version found more. An audit after the deadline, then four independent reviewers, removed the ones that rested on one upload probe, a reader that listed the writer's own token and calls cut inside their verb. Most of the rest have an anonymous run on one side: a record with no token and no name. [[c3|Only {named} are between two named tokens, across {named_pairs} sender and receiver pairs.]]

[[c4|The earliest of the {named} is on {rec:R0006786.time}.]] {rec:R0006584.actor} posts to a Hugging Face dataset. Hours later {rec:R0006786.actor} fetches from it. [[c5|At that moment {share_tok} of the dated harmful actions were still to come.]] If this was the first time two agents talked, a warning then would have been early. The version before this one counted an upload by {rec:R0005366.actor} and a download by {rec:R0005421.actor} as the first; the upload turned out to be a probe of a file that already existed, so it is no longer counted.

But a token is not an agent. One agent can hold several tokens. [[c6|The tool's evidence says {rec:R0006584.actor} and {rec:R0006786.actor} belong to the same agent.]] Both tokens appear inside the same records. Both use the same self-chosen place names. Both run the same rare programs. The tool merges {agent_a_tokens} tokens into one estimated agent and calls it Agent A.

[[c7|Counted by estimated agent, {inside} of the {named} deliveries stay inside one agent.]] An agent that reads its own file is not coordination. That leaves {between} deliveries between different agents.

[[c8|The first delivery between two different agents is on {rec:R0045143.time}.]] {rec:R0044824.actor} commits to a dataset. A little over an hour later {rec:R0045143.actor}, one of Agent A's tokens, reads it. [[c9|By then only {share_agent} of the dated harmful actions were still to come.]] The same sign that looked early now looks late.

Not very, and a reader should know why. [[c10|Every time in this story is estimated.]] The release has no time field for these records, so the tool dates them from timestamps the agents wrote into their code. [[c11|The tool also grades its own deliveries by how it found the verbs. All of them are graded weak.]]

[[c12|One reader, the authors' AI assistant, labelled all {audited} named deliveries with a helper script and judged {audited_true} of them a real write and a later read.]] That is one reader, once; no person read them by hand and nobody labelled them a second time, and the labels were changed in the same commit as the rule they score. The merge into Agent A is an estimate too. If the merge is wrong, the earlier date stands.

c12.caveat: One reader, one pass, and the labels for 13 links were changed in the same commit as the rule. The audit says nothing about true deliveries the tool missed.

c13.evidence: Deliveries where the reader's record shares identifiers, paths or file names with the writer's record (the written-content test).
c13.caveat: A shared term is not proof of use, and no shared term is not proof of non-use. The test is deliberately strict.
